fields.statement: Verifier claude-code-7712db35 at 5eb92da1 (builder commit only tracks its actor record; the code landed in b187f837): go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(run-autonomy-source|describe-golden|workflow-plan-autonomy)$' passes. run-autonomy-source.txtar starts a run of a workflow declaring [autonomy] plan = "auto" with accept undeclared and git config rhiza.autonomy.accept owner; run start and run status print '- Autonomy plan: auto from workflow declares' and '- Autonomy accept: owner from rhiza.autonomy.accept'; run status --json carries stage/mode/source/workflow; the journal's started entry carries both. describe-golden.txtar includes the autonomy field and passes. Since the script's workflow is a command workflow named declares, I also ran a real plan run by hand with a scratch build in a scratch root (RHIZA_* env cleared): .rhiza/workflows/plan.toml = builtin plan.toml + [autonomy] plan = "auto", rhiza.autonomy.accept owner; rhiza run start --workflow plan --new Exports --dry-run --permission-mode manual printed 'Autonomy plan: auto from workflow plan' and 'Autonomy accept: owner from rhiza.autonomy.accept' (plus ship/signoff from settings). Read internal/api/autonomy.go runAutonomy: workflow declaration first, naming the workflow, else rhiza.autonomy.<stage>; recorded in run.Started.Autonomy.
